remedies.title: Check the policy dates on your schedule
remedies.body: The admission date falls outside the policy period we read. If you renewed, upload the latest schedule. A renewal paid within the grace period keeps cover continuous, but claims for treatment during the unpaid gap itself may not be paid.

remedies.title: Ask the insurer or TPA to confirm cover
remedies.body: Call the number on your health card and ask whether the policy is in force on the planned admission date. Ask them to note the call reference.

remedies.title: Add the policy start and end dates
remedies.body: Upload your policy schedule, or type the start and end dates exactly as printed on it, so the policy period can be checked.

remedies.title: Add the planned admission date
remedies.body: Enter the admission date from the hospital estimate or the doctor's advice so it can be compared with the policy period.

remedies.title: Tell the insurer if this is due to an accident
remedies.body: The initial waiting period does not apply to claims arising from an accident. If the treatment is because of an accident, say so truthfully with the supporting medical records.

remedies.title: Check whether earlier cover counts
remedies.body: If you ported or migrated from another policy without a break, your first inception date is the earlier policy's start date. Upload the porting or previous policy documents.

remedies.title: Plan non-urgent treatment after the waiting period
remedies.body: If your doctor says the treatment can safely wait, the waiting period ends on the date shown in this check. Medical advice comes first; never delay emergency care.

remedies.title: Add the first inception date
remedies.body: The schedule usually prints 'Date of first inception' or 'Continuous cover since'. Upload it or type the date so the waiting period can be checked.

remedies.title: Say whether the treatment is due to an accident
remedies.body: Inside the waiting period, only accident claims are covered. Answer the accident question on the facts screen as it really happened.

remedies.title: Tell the insurer if the condition is due to an accident
remedies.body: The specific-disease waiting period does not apply to claims arising from an accident. If that is what happened, give the medical records that show it.

remedies.title: Check whether earlier cover counts
remedies.body: Continuous cover from a previous policy you ported or migrated from counts towards this waiting period. Upload the previous policy schedule.

remedies.title: Ask your doctor whether the treatment can wait
remedies.body: Planned procedures on the waiting-period list are covered once the period ends, on the date shown here. Follow your doctor's advice about timing.

remedies.title: Add the diagnosis or planned procedure
remedies.body: Upload the hospital estimate or the doctor's advice note, or type the diagnosis as written by the doctor, so it can be compared with the waiting-period list.

remedies.title: Add the first inception date
remedies.body: The waiting period counts from the first policy with continuous cover. Add that date from your schedule.

remedies.title: Check the PED waiting period end date
remedies.body: Claims for a pre-existing disease are covered once the waiting period on your schedule ends. The date is shown in this check; plan non-urgent care with your doctor.

remedies.title: Check when the condition was first diagnosed
remedies.body: If your medical records show the condition was first diagnosed after the policy started, it is not a pre-existing disease. Correct the date on the facts screen only if your records show it.

remedies.title: Check whether earlier cover counts
remedies.body: Time on a previous policy you ported or migrated from counts towards the PED waiting period. Upload the previous policy schedule.

remedies.title: Answer the pre-existing disease question
remedies.body: Say whether the person had this condition, or symptoms of it, before the policy started, and when it was first diagnosed, exactly as your medical records show.

remedies.title: Check the schedule for declared conditions
remedies.body: Many schedules list declared pre-existing diseases. Upload the schedule so the facts can be read from it.

remedies.title: Talk to the insurer about the undisclosed condition
remedies.body: A condition that existed before the policy and was not declared can lead to a rejection. Speak to the insurer or your agent before admission and give full, accurate medical history.

remedies.title: Know when the moratorium starts
remedies.body: After the moratorium period of continuous cover shown in this check, a claim can be contested only for proven fraud. This check shows the date it begins.

remedies.title: Get independent help
remedies.body: If a claim is rejected, write to the insurer's grievance officer, then use Bima Bharosa or the Insurance Ombudsman. Keep copies of every document.

remedies.title: Choose a room within your policy's limit
remedies.body: A room above the limit also cuts associated charges in proportion. A room within the cap removes this deduction: ask the hospital for its room tariff and which rooms fall within your limit. If your doctor says you need ICU, do not change the room for cover; ask what an ICU day costs.

remedies.title: Ask whether the hospital uses room-based billing
remedies.body: The wording says proportionate deduction is not applied to expenses for which the hospital does not bill differently by room category. Ask the hospital billing desk in writing.

remedies.title: Check for a higher sum insured or room upgrade at renewal
remedies.body: The room limit depends on your sum insured. At renewal, compare a higher sum insured or a plan without a room cap; this does not help the current admission.

remedies.title: Add the room rent per day and number of days
remedies.body: Upload the hospital estimate, or type the room category, rent per day and expected days, so the room limit can be checked.

remedies.title: Ask the hospital for an itemised estimate
remedies.body: An estimate split into room, nursing, surgeon, OT, implants, pharmacy and diagnostics lets the room-rent rule be applied line by line.

remedies.title: Budget for the co-payment
remedies.body: This policy has a co-payment for this person's age at entry. It applies to every claim; plan for it before admission.

remedies.title: Check other cover you may have
remedies.body: An employer group policy or another personal policy may cover the co-payment part. Tell both insurers about each other, as their claim forms ask.

remedies.title: Add the age at entry
remedies.body: The schedule prints the insured person's age or date of birth at entry. Add it so the co-payment can be checked.

remedies.title: Upload the policy schedule
remedies.body: Age at entry is usually on the first page of the schedule, next to the insured person's name.

remedies.title: Ask about restoration or recharge benefits
remedies.body: Some plans restore the sum insured after it is used up. Ask the insurer whether a restoration or recharge applies to this admission.

remedies.title: Use other cover for the balance
remedies.body: An employer group policy or a top-up policy can pay the amount above your sum insured. Tell each insurer about the other.

remedies.title: Plan the amount above the sum insured
remedies.body: The estimate is above the sum insured left this year. Ask the hospital about package rates, and plan how you will pay the difference.

remedies.title: Add the sum insured
remedies.body: Upload the policy schedule or type the sum insured as printed on it.

remedies.title: Add any claims already paid this year
remedies.body: If a claim was already paid this policy year, enter the amount so the remaining sum insured is right. Enter 0 if none.
